result.rationale: The diff clearly shows `catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` discarding the caught error and the handler then returning `{ message: "Guests added" }`. This is a deliberate best-effort email pattern (matching sendLocationChangeEmails-style resilience), so it is not strictly a correctness defect introduced by the change, but it is a specific, substantive concern: on SMTP/template failure the mutation reports success, guests are added to the DB but never notified, and production logs contain neither the error message nor stack, making the failure undiagnosable. judged_text: The catch block discards the caught error object and logs only the literal string 'Error sending AddGuestsEmails'. When guest-notification emails fail (SMTP outage, template crash), production logs carry no reason and no stack while the mutation still returns success - the operator cannot diagnose why guests never heard anything.

adjudication.rationale: In `addGuests.handler.ts`, the email send is wrapped in `try { await sendAddGuestsEmails(...) } catch (err) { console.log("Error sending AddGuestsEmails"); }` which (a) discards the caught `err` object/stack and (b) continues to return success (`return { message: "Guests added" };`) even if email delivery fails. This is a concrete, diff-grounded observability/operability gap introduced by the change, though not necessarily a hard correctness defect if emails are intended to be best-effort.
